nodes.description: The recurrent type 1 and type 2 alleles are distinct, partially overlapping 34-bp deletions in the TXNL4A promoter. They disrupt a region containing two 22-bp repeats separated by a 12-bp spacer; there is no single 56-bp pathogenic deletion. These regulatory alterations are distinct from coding, splice-site and copy-number loss on the other allele. Most BMKS genotypes combine a type 1 deletion with a loss-of-function allele; homozygous promoter deletions also occur.

evidence.snippet: In 8 families, affected individuals carried a rare loss-of-function mutation (nonsense, frameshift, or microdeletion) on one allele and a low-frequency 34 bp deletion (allele frequency 0.76%) in the core promoter region on the other allele.

nodes.description: A hypomorphic promoter allele combined with a coding, splice or copy-number loss-of-function allele reduces functional TXNL4A dosage. Patient-derived iPSCs and neural crest cells have reduced TXNL4A RNA. Total RNA is not equivalent to functional protein: several coding-mutant transcripts escape nonsense-mediated decay, and the unaffected mother carrying a frameshift had unchanged total RNA. Complete human biallelic null lethality is hypothesized from conserved model-organism function, not demonstrated in humans.

evidence.reference_title: TXNL4A-Related Craniofacial Disorders.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of a TXNL4A-related craniofacial disorder is established in a proband with suggestive findings and biallelic pathogenic variants in TXNL4A identified by molecular genetic testing. All probands described to date have had at least one copy of one of the two partially overlapping 34-bp deletions in the TXNL4A promoter.

nodes.description: Unilateral translation-blocking morpholino injection at the two-cell stage reduces neural crest markers, increases dorsal ectodermal apoptosis at neurula stage 15, and produces cranial cartilage defects in 38% of stage-45 tadpoles. This transient knockdown does not reproduce the human promoter-plus-loss-of-function genotype and does not establish dominant inheritance or p53 dependence.
